tb21_profile.skill: Implement a CPU/ISA emulator from spec: load an ELF image, decode fixed-width instructions, maintain registers/PC/memory, and emulate the Linux syscall interface well enough to run a real program
tb21_profile.domain: Low-level systems / computer architecture: MIPS ISA, ELF binaries, Linux syscall ABI, JavaScript (Node.js) as host language
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec, large and open-ended, verified by running a real workload (doom boots, first frame rendered)

searches: tools.py words all opcode register "program counter" interpreter "virtual machine" -n 40
tools.py search rts 'Brainfuck|brainfuck|interpreter for|write an interpreter|emulator' -n 30
tools.py words smith parser tokenizer "abstract syntax" grammar "state machine" evaluate -n 30
tools.py search rebench 'bytecode|opcode|instruction set|virtual machine|dis\.dis|CPython interpreter|stack frame' -n 25
tools.py show d0c-s4vage__pfp-109 d0c-s4vage__pfp-114 d0c-s4vage__pfp-116 d0c-s4vage__pfp-126 d0c-s4vage__pfp-128

TMax-15K.reason: Write a C interpreter for 32-bit fixed-width register bytecode from a written ISA spec: registers, PC, relative jumps, sign extension, file output.
Complete a 4-byte-instruction register VM decoding opcode/operand fields from a bytecode file; fuzzed against a reference implementation like the doom trace.
Implement a C bytecode interpreter reading little-endian 32-bit immediates from a byte stream and matching an oracle VM byte-for-byte.
Reverse-engineer a stripped stack-machine binary's instruction set, then reimplement the emulator natively with identical output and error behaviour.
Implement a register VM in C++ that parses and executes a custom assembly language with an instruction-count quota; same fetch-decode-execute loop.
Assemble instructions into exact little-endian binary bytecode then emulate the stack machine over that byte stream: encode plus decode, both sides.
Implement an emulator for an assembly instruction set and register file recovered from a spec document; same build-an-interpreter-from-ISA-description work.
Reimplement a bytecode interpreter (8-bit accumulator, wrapping arithmetic, operand fetch, halt) to exactly match a stripped reference binary.
Parse ELF directly in C - magic, class, PT_GNU_STACK program headers, dynamic tags - which is the loader half of running a MIPS ELF.
Reverse-engineer a stripped binary and write a bit-exact reimplementation verified by mass fuzzing; same replicate-observed-machine-semantics discipline.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Walk process loading, user-mode entry and the write syscall in GDB, then validate captured state - exactly the kernel/user boundary a syscall emulator must model.
ARM64 assembly using only raw Linux syscalls, no libc: forces explicit register and syscall-ABI reasoning, the same semantics vm.js must implement.
Verify and correct syscall numbers against the real ARM64 Linux ABI before assembling; teaches that syscall tables are per-arch, a MIPS-interpreter trap.
ARM64 program needing syscall numbers and the exact stack layout at process entry - the argv/stack setup an ELF loader in vm.js must reproduce.
Write libc-free ARM64 assembly doing file IO via syscalls, verify it is a static ELF, and run it under a user-mode emulator.
Patch a compiled executable's bytes in place to change its output: requires reading binary layout rather than source, like loading a MIPS image.
Debugger walkthrough of process setup, transfer to user mode and syscall handling; builds the mental model of the machine state an interpreter tracks.
Cross-assemble ARM64, run under a user-mode emulator, and script a rebuild/verify harness; touches emulation tooling but writes no interpreter.
Two C Brainfuck interpreters to build, run and lint: same interpreter-loop code in view, but the work is static analysis, not implementation.
Build an ARM64 binary and produce a disassembly listing proving the write syscall is present; reading machine code back from bytes, but shallow.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Emulate a binary for the custom dan32 architecture in radare2 ESIL, driving registers/memory by hand and wiring an external interrupt handler - CPU emulation with traps.
Set up an ESIL VM, initialise stack and registers, and emulate x86 code instruction by instruction; same machine-state bookkeeping as an interpreter loop.
Step an ELF parser under LLDB while it chews a MIPS busybox program header - literally ELF program-header parsing for a MIPS binary.
Assemble, link, then single-step the first instructions under GDB inspecting register state - the per-instruction execution model vm.js must reproduce.
Build a non-PIE ELF and let an assembly virus rewrite its headers/segments; requires understanding ELF segment layout and entry point.
Patch PT_INTERP inside an ELF and control dynamic loading - direct experience of the ELF structures an interpreter must read to map segments.
Analyse an ELF crackme and bypass it by manipulating CPU flags at runtime; forces explicit reasoning about processor state and conditional execution.
Record and deterministically replay a guest program under the QEMU i386 system emulator - whole-system emulation and reproducible execution traces.
Compile and run two C Brainfuck interpreters and compare them under a static analyser; interpreter code is present but not authored.
Build a language runtime into a wasm module runnable from Node.js: same host (Node) executing a foreign instruction format, but the toolchain does the work.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Fix a CCITT G4 decoder producing wrong bit patterns and cursor positions - bit-level state-machine decoding of a binary stream, same care as instruction decode.
Restore the LZW decoder's run loop so a byte stream decodes to exact expected bytes; implementing a documented decoding algorithm from its definition.
Implement missing type-2 xref-stream entry handling: decoding packed binary offset records into object/index/generation fields.
Fix DER encoding so components serialise in tag order - exact byte-level output of a binary encoding with strict format rules.
Repair PDFXRefStream.get_entry field unpacking; recovering structured records from a packed binary table, the same work as ELF section parsing.
Fix char-width lookup inside PDFPageInterpreter, the content-stream interpreter; debugging an operand-dispatch interpreter against expected output.
Sequence decoder drops/reorders fields and the boolean encoder is wrong: codec round-trip correctness over a typed binary schema.
asOctets reverses byte order, corrupting encodings - endianness bugs are the classic failure mode when decoding MIPS words from an image.
CCITTFaxDecoder.output_line uses a buffer before defining it; control-flow repair inside a per-row bit decoder.
Fix NodeVisitor dispatch in a PEG engine: table-driven dispatch over node types is the same shape as an opcode dispatch table.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: pfp is an interpreter that parses binaries; fix implicit-array semantics so a real DEX template with uleb128 decoding matches the reference implementation.
Make boolean short-circuiting lazily resolve variable references in the interpreter - correcting evaluation-order semantics against a reference machine.
Implicit duplicate arrays must resolve through scope as well as struct children; scope/name-resolution work inside a binary-parsing interpreter.
Implement the missing Memcmp builtin in the interpreter's function table - adding an unimplemented operation, exactly what unhandled MIPS syscalls need.
Chained assignment a = b = c unsupported: implement the missing expression-evaluation rule in the interpreter's node handlers.
Enum fields fail on parse/set_val: type handling where interpreter values are backed by bytes read from the input stream.
Parameterised typedef'd structs in the binary template language - parameter passing in the interpreter's declaration handling.
Compiler must reject mutating arrays nested in complex types during iteration; reasoning about lowered machine semantics rather than surface syntax.
Add __iter__ over the parsed binary DOM; same codebase and data model as the stronger pfp items but a trivial API change.
Scale/offset handling when reading packed LAS point records; binary record decoding, but the bug is arithmetic policy, not format parsing.

final_top10.reason: Write a register-machine interpreter in C from a written ISA spec: PC, registers, fixed 32-bit encoding, relative jumps, sign extension, file output.
Build a 4-byte-instruction VM decoding opcode and register fields from a bytecode file, fuzz-compared against a reference implementation.
C bytecode interpreter over a raw byte stream with little-endian immediates that must match an oracle VM on arbitrary input.
Reverse-engineer a stripped emulator's instruction set and reimplement it natively with identical stdout and error behaviour.
Implement a two-register VM in C++ that parses and executes a custom assembly language with an execution quota and exit-code contract.
Encode instructions to exact little-endian bytecode and then emulate that byte stream - both halves of the assemble/execute pipeline.
Implement an emulator for an assembly instruction set and register file taken from a spec document, then report final register state.
Emulate a custom-architecture binary under radare2 ESIL with an external interrupt handler and manual register/memory manipulation.
Reimplement a bytecode interpreter (operand fetch, wrapping 8-bit ALU, halt semantics) to match a stripped reference binary exactly.
Fix interpreter semantics in pfp, a binary-template interpreter, so a DEX template with uleb128 decoding matches the reference implementation.

notes: Lexical retrieval was badly off for this task: the TMax shortlist was dominated by ffmpeg/video-frame boilerplate ('save the frames as they are rendered' collided with dozens of video-extraction chores) and none of my top six TMax picks were in the shown list - all came from my own searches for emulator/opcode/bytecode/register. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has no interpreter-implementation task at all; its best offer is raw ARM64 syscall assembly and GDB syscall walkthroughs, so ranks 7-10 there are weak and should be treated as filler. SWE-Smith likewise has nothing shaped like this; I judged it purely on binary-decoding skill (pdfminer CCITT/LZW/xref, pyasn1 DER) and its task_form scores are honestly 2. The strongest non-TMax find is the d0c-s4vage/pfp family in SWE-Rebench (8 tasks) - pfp is an interpreter for a C-like binary-template language, so both 'implement missing interpreter semantics' and 'parse a binary format' transfer; six of them are defensible, the last two are padding. Note tw_18948 is the only corpus task that touches MIPS directly (an ELF parser on busybox-mips-phdr), but it is an LLDB session, not an implementation.
